2609.10123.title: If It's Not Buggy, Don't Fix It: On the Dynamics of Iterative Bug-fixing with LLMs
2609.10123.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) have become ubiquitous in software development, with LLM-based automated program repair tools increasingly used during code review. In this report, we explore the iterative blind use of LLMs as bug-fixers. Across multiple models and repair environments, we find that LLMs consistently claim to detect bugs in entirely bug-free programs while the rate of repair of buggy programs is less than that of the damage to correct programs. We also explore the long-term dynamics of this iterative process, and find that this frequently reaches a pseudo-bug-fixing cycle where the same changes are added and removed again ad infinitum. Lastly, via mechanistic probing, we unveil the existence of a steering vector which controls the editing propensity, suggesting that LLMs have an internal representation of ``buggy code", and that this representation is what is falsely activated to induce pseudo-bug fixing. These results provide insight towards the dynamics of fully autonomous bug-fixing systems, as well as stopping conditions under ambiguous goals.
2609.10123.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在軟體開發中已變得無處不在，基於LLM的自動程式修復工具在程式碼審查過程中越來越常被使用。<lb/>在本報告中，我們探討了LLMs作為錯誤修復者的迭代盲目使用。<lb/>在多個模型和修復環境中，我們發現LLMs持續聲稱能在完全無錯誤的程式中檢測到錯誤，而修復有錯誤的程式的比率則低於對正確程式造成的損害。<lb/>我們還探討了這一迭代過程的長期動態，發現這經常達到一種偽錯誤修復循環，其中相同的更改不斷被添加和移除，無限循環。<lb/>最後，通過機械探測，我們揭示了一個控制編輯傾向的引導向量的存在，這表明LLMs對“有錯誤的程式碼”有內部表示，而這種表示被錯誤激活以誘發偽錯誤修復。<lb/>這些結果提供了對完全自動錯誤修復系統動態的洞察，以及在模糊目標下的停止條件。
